1.sofaString: 347	Pt, *****, is a 21 year old male who is diagnosed with hypoplastic left heart syndrome s/p fontan with PLE being referred for heart transplant Psychosocial Assessment.  Information for this assessment was obtained through an interview with the pt's mother and aunt and review of the medical records.   SW did not speak to ***** at this time as mother requested that he not participate in transplant discussions until it is more likely that he will be listed.  She disclosed that he tends to perseverate on things that he is anxious about.  SW spent 75 minutes of face to face time with patient's family.     Living situation:  **, *****, lives with his parents in ************, *******.  They just recently relocated into a different home in the same subdivision.  They moved into a corner lot with more property and privacy, as well as more room for ***** to have more of his own space.  Mom reports that ***** loves the new house.  The house has central heating and a/c.  They replace the air filters monthly.  They have city water.  There is no smoking in the home.  They have a dog (medium size ***** mix), a bird, and a ***** (that is kept in the garage).         Demographics:  Mother: ******** ******  DOB:  **/**/****           Age:  49  Employment:  Had been working as a manager at a hair[SM1] *****.  However, she does not plan to return to work in order to stay home with ***** and monitor his compliance with fluid restrictions etc  Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Father: ***** ******  Employment:  Works at **** and Associates   Phone:  ***-***-**** (cell)     Siblings:  Brother:  ******* ******, age 23.  Resides in ****** **** *****      Aunt:  ****** ****  ******* in ******, **.  Works for **** Hotels administration  Phone:  ***-***-****     Support systems:  ******** reports that she and her husband provide support for one another.  She states her sister (******) is also a big support. Although she lives in ******, she is actively involved in their lives and is able to come to assist them when needed.  She has been present for the last week during this admission and is participating in this evaluation, but will be returning to ***** this weekend.   ****** was tearful when talking about the need to return to ******. She disclosed that she has only been in ****** about a year and a half.  She moved there for her '***** job'.  However, she states she is really close to her family and misses them.     Parents report that ***** is very close with his parents.  He does not like to be alone while in the hospital.  Prior to this admission, he was able to stay home by himself while mom was at work. He would cook dinner and have it waiting when they came home from work.  However, he was not on a fluid restriction at the time.  Now that he is on a fluid restriction, ***** cannot be left alone at all as he will drink excessive amounts of fluid if no one is watching.  While in the hospital, he reports drinking about 8000 ml of water in the shower.         The family denies that transportation is a problem.  Both parents own their own vehicle.  ******** states they are able to afford the gas expenses as well.  Because she feels the need to stay in the room with him at the hospital, she denies that displacement lodging expenses will be a problem either.  She also denies need for assistance with displacement food expenses.  Fundraising through **** was  encouraged.  However, she verbalizes that they do not need financial assistance at this time. ******** states they would likely commute back and forth for follow up appts after transplant if this were allowed.  If not, she believes they would be able to afford displacement lodging temporarily.        ***** is not in school.  He did not graduate.  He has completed a 9th grade level of education.  He has not participated in any vocational skills training.  He has *********** at the zoo and at a restaurant previously.  He likes animals.  ******** is considering the possibility of them both volunteering at the humane society.       Course of illness:        ***** was born with hypoplastic left heart syndrome.  He had ******* at 8 days old, glenn at 6 mo old, and fontan at 19 mo of age.  He developed protein losing enteropathy at age 5.  This was successfully managed medically until about 2 years ago.  He has had 3 admissions over the past 2 years for fluid overload and hypoalbuminemia.  He was most recently admitted to ******** on */*/** with electrolyte imbalances that likely contributed to a seizure on */*/**.  He was transferred to us for heart transplant evaluation on */*/**.      Financial Situation:     ***** is covered by Medicaid ****** insurance.  He receives social security benefits as well.  Due to his developmental and intellectual delays, the parents are his legal decision makers.  In the event that they are unable to provide consent, Aunt ****** would be the next person to provide consent.  The family is supported primarily by dad's employment income.  ******** was also working part-time, but they did not depend on her income.  She does not plan to resume working and they verbalize that there will be no financial stress related to this.  The family does not verbalize a need to ********* at this time.              Family History:     There is no other major family medical history.  The maternal grandfather had triple bypass surgery but was in 70's at the time.  The great grandmother had diabetes.  There is no other heart related history.  There is no cancer in the family history.        In regards to mental health history, ***** has been reportedly diagnosed with anxiety.  The only psychotropic medication he has been prescribed was Zoloft, prior to this admission.  During this admission, ***** demonstrated aggressive behaviors and hallucinations.  Psychiatry saw him and put him on *********.  He also had to be given Haldol a few times in order to get his behavior under control.  It is believed this was secondary to electrolyte imbalance rather than a psychiatric condition.  ******** reports that she had never previously seen him exhibit behavior like that.  He also has a history of sleep disturbances.  He can go for days on end without sleeping.  Several things were tried during this admission.  It seems he has been tolerating ambien ok for help with sleep.       ******** also reports that she gets migraines when she is sleep deprived.  She has been prescribed Elavil for this.       ******** denies any substance abuse in the immediate family.  However, she reports that her father was an alcoholic in the past.  There is no reported history of DV or involvement with DCF or law enforcement.       Adherence:  There are several concerns related to adherence.  One concern is *****'s inability to regulate his fluid intake.  ******** reports that he had been taking in *-* liters of fluid per day previously.  He is now on fluid restrictions, but has been found to sneak liquids at any opportunity he can (including drinking shower water).      In addition, ***** cannot take pills.  The majority of his medications are given through his g-tube.  ******** does not think he will be able to take prograf capsules by mouth.  It was explained that prograf should not be administered through g-tube.  In addition, it is difficult to get financial approval for liquid prograf for an adult patient.  ******** states they will work on this issue, but she does not feel confident he can take a pill or capsule.       Another concern is that there have been multiple times when ***** has pulled off his leads and attempted to remove his lines etc.  He has also threatened to leave the hospital ***.  Although this is unlikely with his mother at bedside, these behaviors could make managing him post-operatively more complicated.       ******** denies that there will be any difficulty keeping follow up appointments, obtaining labs, etc.       Assessment and recommendations:     ******** admits that she is overwhelmed with thinking about the prospect of transplant.  However, she is equally afraid of trying to manage him medically at home as his electrolytes and albumin levels have been so difficult to maintain at a therapeutic level.  She states ***** would likely be in agreement with a transplant if it meant he could drink without restrictions.  She states they will do whatever it takes to keep him healthy.                              IMPRESSION:     (Low Risk - 1; Moderate Risk - 2; High Risk - 3; Severe Risk - 4)     Home Environment/Transportation -  1     Family Background & Social Support -  1     Financial/Insurance  - 1     Mental Health/Substance Abuse - 2     Involvement with *** Enforcement/Child Protection -  1     Adherence - 3     Understanding of medical situation & transplant process -  2     Health Literacy -  2     Coping Skills - 3     Total:  16  Moderate     The family scores as moderate risk in regards to psychosocial contra-indicators to transplant.       The primary concerns are the issues with compliance with fluid restrictions and the difficulty ***** has  with taking oral medications.  Recommendations are listed below:     Recommendations:  *Provide ongoing education in simple terms to the family about heart transplant and post-transplant care.  Use teach-back method to ensure that the family/ patient are understanding what is being explained.  *Assist with connecting patient and family with counseling and supports that will assist in positive coping skills   *Assist ***** in reducing aversion and anxiety related to taking oral medications by engaging Child **** and positive reinforcement/ reward system.       ****** ******** LCSW  Pediatric Heart/ Lung Transplant Team  ***-***-****[SM1]occupation
